children: Paramount Skydance has reportedly cleared the last major hurdle to its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by reaching a settlement with California and 11 other states that sued over antitrust concerns.

A settlement would remove a key obstacle for $110 billion megamerger of the two entertainment giants. Warners Bros. Discovery shares surged 10% to $30.57 on the reports, erasing all its losses for the year. Paramount shares rose nearly 9% to $111.12 in recent Monday trading.
Neither company nor California's Attorney General Rob Bonta replied to Barron's request for comment.

The suit, filed in July, claims that the merger would "extinguish competition" between Paramount and Warner Bros. film studios and "inflict substantial harm" on movie theaters, cable distributors, and moviegoers.
The Wall Street Journal and other media outlets reported the settlement late Monday morning.

The media companies originally announced their merger in February after Paramount outbid rival Netflix for Warner Bros. Netflix had originally offered $82.7 billion for Warner Bros., and Paramount agreed to pay a $2.8 billion termination fee when the deal fell through.
